clue.text: Crooked horse-trader offered his

parts.note: the hunchbacked Richard III in Shakespeare cries out that he would trade his realm for a horse

explanation.surface: A bent dealer in horses puts up something of his own as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests a dishonest dealer, but it means hunchbacked: Shakespeare's Richard III shouts 'A horse! A horse! My ... for a horse!'
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III offered his realm, the land he ruled as monarch, in exchange for a horse.

clue.text: Start to remove shoes

definitions.meaning: the opening moment of a football match, the whistle that begins play
to fling footwear off with a flick of the feet

explanation.surface: Getting going by taking one's footwear off.
explanation.definitionFit: A football match begins with its kick-off, and you can kick off your shoes by flicking them from your feet.

clue.text: No one in New York

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the clue says one is in New York

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dollar'

explanation.surface: Nobody at all lives in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old-fashioned or formal synonym for a refusal, used in voting.

clue.text: Obedient union leader used to negotiate

indicators.note: to negotiate a deal is to work it out anew, so these letters are reworked
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A compliant trade union boss was used to carry out talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to negotiate' signals the anagram of U (the first letter of 'union') plus USED.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is a literary synonym for dutiful, describing someone who does what they are told.

clue.text: One to long for honey

parts.note: one, the impersonal pronoun, can stand for me, the speaker
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honey' looks like a term of endearment, but it is honey the food: MEL is its Latin and pharmacy name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel is the Latin word for the sweet stuff bees make, still used in pharmacy.

clue.text: See 27
Notice smelly problem's in remission. Ace, potentially!

indicators.note: a disease in remission is going back, so the letters for the smelly problem run backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a smelly problem
in tennis an ace is a kind of serve that the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: Spot that body odour has eased off; perhaps it is a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: A disease 'in remission' is in retreat, hence the reversal; the 's after 'problem' is a link and 'potentially' marks a serve as one kind of ace.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to watch or perceive it, a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Flog fruit to Germany, Spain and everyone French

parts.note: to flog goods is to tout them, sell them pushily
a lemon is a fruit
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A trader hawks fruit across Germany and Spain to all French people.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means literally 'all the world', i.e. everybody.

clue.text: Neil wanders the streets getting signs up

indicators.note: something that wanders roams off course, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ST is short for street, so STS is streets

explanation.surface: Neil roams the town making gestures overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' rearranges NEIL to ENLI; 'the' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for the army joins it, which is to enlist.

clue.text: King Canute finally turned back the receding tide

definitions.text: King Canute finally turned back the receding tide

parts.words: King Canute finally turned back the receding tide
parts.note: the legend says Canute could not hold back the sea, but the outgoing water goes back on its own

explanation.surface: The legendary king at last succeeds in holding back the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute failed to stop the tide coming in; the only sea that 'turns back' is one already going out.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the outflow of the sea after high water, the receding phase of the tide.

clue.text: Camilla initially taking nothing from good man in royal palace perhaps

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter
the good man is placed inside the remaining letters
taking nothing from a word removes the O from it

parts.note: taken as the word itself
O looks like zero, nothing
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Camilla, getting nothing from a decent fellow, stays in a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' removes the O (nothing) from ROYAL and 'in' puts the saint inside; 'palace perhaps' points to London's Crystal Palace, the great glass exhibition hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crystal Palace was the great glass hall of the 1851 Exhibition, so this is one kind of palace.

clue.text: Brainbox's expertise with current university exchange

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another, as the clue tells us to swap them

parts.note: skill means expertise
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A clever person's know-how combines with a modern student exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brainbox' is usually a clever person, but here it is the bony box holding the brain; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium is literally the case enclosing the brain, a box of bone.

clue.text: See 27
Dastard lied! Dreadful 0 A E fibs!

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A villain is accused of telling awful lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges DASTARD LIED. The letters '0 A E' are print debris, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Taradiddles are petty lies or pretentious nonsense, an old word for minor untruths.

clue.text: Or the alternative

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of these letters gives the answer

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A simple choice between two options.
explanation.definitionFit: Different or remaining is what this word means, the choice that is not this one.

clue.text: Thanks to Henry for S K E tipping it?

definitions.text: Thanks to Henry for S K E tipping it?

indicators.note: tipping over turns something upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A gesture of gratitude to a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipping' reverses TA + H; the whole clue is the &lit picture of tipping your headwear as thanks. The letters 'S K E' are print debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's bonnet or cap is a traditional gesture of thanks or greeting.

clue.text: Keep going the French way

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Carry on the way they do in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or continue is a sense of the verb, as in 'it will not survive the winter'.

clue.text: South-eastern service: return ticket prices

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A southern English rail company sets the price of a return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses SE + RAF; 'return ticket' looks like a railway phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers pay set charges for travel; these are the costs of tickets.

clue.text: Mother's broken flask

indicators.note: broken up and put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S

explanation.surface: Mum's vacuum bottle has smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot or cold; the brand name became the generic word.

clue.text: State where William was conceived?

definitions.meaning: Prince William was conceived inside his mother, Princess Diana

explanation.surface: Asking about the place where a prince began his life.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as IN DIANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern US state, and split up it says William's mother Diana held him.

clue.text: Marriage vow: to fib O J A A N about last of lovers .. and worship!

parts.note: 'I do' is the vow spoken at a wedding

indicators.note: fib is placed around the letter, as about means surrounding

parts.note: a lie is a fib

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A wedding promise: lying about one's partner, and devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S, the last letter of 'lovers', inside LIE. The letters 'O J A A N' are print debris.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to idolise them; a synonym, both verbs.

clue.text: Tough sheilas from Australia, heading north in a bloke's …

indicators.note: Australia's letters go inside 'a bloke's'

parts.note: a bloke is a man, so a man's

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Oz is a slang name for Australia

explanation.surface: Hardy Australian women ride north in a man's off-roader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' means reading upwards. Sheila is Australian slang for a woman, and the clue runs on into 21 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were mythical warrior women, so the word means strong, formidable women.

clue.text: See 27
Musical Carmen: Bach penned a number

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: JS are the initials of Johann Sebastian Bach
one is a number

explanation.surface: A musical work: Bach composed a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'wrote', but means enclosed. Carmen Jones is the Hammerstein musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen Jones is a 1943 Broadway show, so this surname completes the title of the musical.

clue.text: …4x4, not quietly doughnut-scoffing

indicators.note: not means the quiet letter is left out

parts.note: a Jeep is a four-wheel-drive vehicle
p (piano) means quietly in music
a ring is the shape of a doughnut

explanation.surface: Loudly eating a doughnut in an off-roader.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 19 down. 'scoffing' looks like eating greedily, but means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock, and jeering is the same derisive behaviour.

clue.text: Suppresses issue of trouble and strife perhaps

definitions.meaning: crushes or quashes, as when you tread on something

definitions.text: issue of trouble and strife perhaps
definitions.meaning: trouble and strife is rhyming slang for wife; her son by an earlier partner

explanation.surface: Quashing the children of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife; the clue's two halves split the answer as STEPS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on is to crush or suppress; a wife's son from an earlier marriage is her husband's stepchild.

clue.text: Low degree of spirit

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Feeling down in the dumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as sad, but is the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit can mean temper or frame of mind, as in 'in high spirits'.

clue.text: Hack off, removing first joint

indicators.note: removing the first letter of the word

parts.note: to hack off is British slang for to annoy, to rankle

explanation.surface: Chopping off part of a leg at the first joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack off' looks like amputate, but is British slang for irritate; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg.

clue.text: English editor coming back to last bit of Milton's Paradise Lost

indicators.note: coming back means going in reverse, so the editor's letters run backwards
the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An English editor returns to the final part of Milton's epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Adam and Eve is the paradise lost in Milton's poem.

clue.text: Cool home with large bathroom that doesn't open

indicators.note: something that doesn't open has lost its opening, the first letter

parts.note: big means large
loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: A trendy house with a huge bathroom whose door won't open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' suggests trendy, but means literally cold: a snow house.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome built of snow blocks is a dwelling that is literally cold.

clue.text: It stars a hero. Ford, 28,is cast

definitions.text: It stars a hero. Ford, 28,is cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and also to mould afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 28 down, the Spanish king's moose

explanation.surface: A film starring Harrison Ford as an action hero is being cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cast' looks like film casting, but signals an anagram of IT STARS A HERO FORD plus ELK.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1981 Spielberg adventure film stars Harrison Ford as the hero Indiana Jones.

clue.text: On the rise according to agent

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per instructions'

explanation.surface: Sales are climbing, the agent says.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative is a travelling agent for a firm.

clue.text: The Spanish king's moose

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
K is short for king in chess notation

explanation.surface: The moose belonging to the King of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the European moose is called by this name.

clue.text: 2 in the audience, one in northern England and no Scots

indicators.note: one is placed inside northern England

parts.note: NE is short for north-east, northern England
a means one

explanation.surface: Two people in the crowd, one from northern England, and no Scots among them.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 in the audience' is a second hint: the answer to 2 down, NAY, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Nae is the Scottish dialect word meaning no or not.

clue.text: Relaxes in quarter on rough seas

parts.note: E is east, one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: rough seas are churned up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds in one part of town despite stormy waters.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax tension is to loosen or lessen it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Babe's family like American football

parts.note: Babe is the pig from the 1995 film, so a pig's
kin means family

explanation.surface: The pig's relatives fancy a game of gridiron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babe' is the pig in the film of that name; 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball in American football was once made of hog hide, so it is called by that nickname.
